notes: French internal flows: real MOBPRO commune-to-commune O-D table. Swiss internal flows: no fine O-D matrix, gravity model hard-constrained to real STATENT employment totals per canton minus real cross-border commuter counts. German internal flows: same gravity approach, constrained to a mix of real (Weil am Rhein, Lörrach) and estimated (other communes, via a jobs/population ratio derived from the two known communes) employment totals — this is the one genuinely estimated component of the pipeline, flagged explicitly rather than presented as sourced. Cross-border flows: real OFS quarterly cross-border commuter statistics, separately for French residents (by department) and German residents (by Landkreis), by canton of work. — Reviewer refinements (2026-08-23), per the multi-nation conservative rule (score the lower-quality nation, here the German side): workplace_count scored estimated_proxy — DE employment totals are real for only two communes (Weil am Rhein, Lörrach) and ratio-estimated everywhere else, the author's own disclosure; the FR (MOBPRO) and CH (STATENT) sides are fully measured but the rule takes the weakest anchor. Workplace grain/placement scored at the weaker FR/DE commune pattern (adm3, mesh_250 × size_only) rather than the filed Swiss 100m claims. Resident resolution pinned to mesh_250 (FR Filosofi is the coarsest of the three measured grids: FR 200m / CH 100m / DE Zensus 100m); resident intensity stays measured_per_unit. O/D kept at structured_marginals @ adm2: the cross-border commuter series (OFS quarterly, by French department and German Landkreis, by canton of work) are real hard totals covering the map's defining flows; the DE-internal gravity over partly-estimated totals is the weak component and is why the pillar is not scored higher.
